officialDocs.label: Snowflake OAuth overview and error codes

verdict.summary: There's no central developer console or app review: Snowflake OAuth clients are security integrations created inside each customer's Snowflake account, so every customer needs an ACCOUNTADMIN (or a role with CREATE INTEGRATION) to run CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION and hand you a client ID and secret. Built-in partner integrations (Tableau, Looker and others) skip that step, but the docs don't describe how a new vendor joins that list.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sign up for a 30-day trial account, create a custom OAuth integration as ACCOUNTADMIN, read the secret with SYSTEM$SHOW_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS, and run the code flow against your account URL.

timeToProd.assumes: Each customer's Snowflake admin creates a custom OAuth security integration for your agent and shares the client credentials; the time per customer depends on how fast their admin acts.
timeToProd.waitingOn: No review needed. Each customer's ACCOUNTADMIN has to create the integration (and may need internal security sign-off).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No Snowflake review exists for custom clients. Customer-side security approval can take far longer and isn't something Snowflake controls.

prerequisites.item: A Snowflake account for development (a 30-day trial works)
prerequisites.why: OAuth integrations live inside an account; there's no account-independent developer console.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The trial page doesn't explicitly say security integrations work in trials; we assume they do.

prerequisites.item: ACCOUNTADMIN, or a role granted CREATE INTEGRATION, in each customer account
prerequisites.why: Only ACCOUNTADMIN has CREATE INTEGRATION by default, and it's needed to create the OAuth integration.

prerequisites.item: A TLS redirect URI with no query parameters
prerequisites.why: Redirect URIs must use TLS unless OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI is set, and the stored URI shouldn't include query parameters.
The authorize (/oauth/authorize) and token (/oauth/token-request) endpoints sit on the customer's own account URL.

scopeTiers.impact: The token is limited to one named role (case-sensitive). Best for an agent that queries a defined set of tables. Add refresh_token for offline access.
Lets the session USE ROLE at runtime. Rejected unless the integration sets OAUTH_ANY_ROLE_MODE to ENABLE or ENABLE_FOR_PRIVILEGE.
ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN, ORGADMIN and GLOBALORGADMIN are blocked by default. Unblocking needs an account parameter change or a Snowflake Support request, which an agent shouldn't need.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=true here means a Support request or account-level change, not an app review.

steps.title: Sign up for a trial account
steps.detail: Create a 30-day Snowflake trial (or use an existing account) and sign in to Snowsight.

steps.title: Generate the integration SQL
steps.detail: Write CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION ... TYPE=OAUTH OAUTH_CLIENT=CUSTOM OAUTH_CLIENT_TYPE='CONFIDENTIAL' OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI='https://...' OAUTH_ISSUE_REFRESH_TOKENS=TRUE OAUTH_ENFORCE_PKCE=TRUE, plus ALLOWED_ROLES_LIST and IS_AGENTIC=TRUE if you want sessions flagged as agent sessions.

steps.title: Create the integration and read the secret
steps.detail: As ACCOUNTADMIN, run the SQL, then SELECT SYSTEM$SHOW_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS('<INTEGRATION_NAME>') to get the client ID and secret. DESCRIBE INTEGRATION shows the endpoints.

steps.title: Implement the code flow per account
steps.detail: Ask the user for their account URL, redirect to <account_url>/oauth/authorize with client_id, response_type=code, redirect_uri, state, scope and a PKCE S256 challenge, then POST form-encoded to <account_url>/oauth/token-request.

steps.title: Connect drivers or the SQL API with the token
steps.detail: Pass the access token to the connector (authenticator=oauth) or the SQL API, and refresh it every ~10 minutes (default access token validity 600 s).

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The authenticator=oauth parameter name is from general Snowflake connector knowledge, not the pages cited.

steps.title: Write customer onboarding instructions
steps.detail: Produce a copy-paste SQL script and a short guide for customer admins: create a dedicated role with least privilege, create the integration with your redirect URI, and send you the client ID/secret securely.

steps.title: Customer admin creates the integration
steps.detail: Each customer's ACCOUNTADMIN runs your script, optionally attaches a NETWORK_POLICY allowing your server IPs, and shares the credentials.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Duration is our estimate, excluding customer-side security review.

steps.title: Schedule refresh-token renewal
steps.detail: Refresh tokens last 90 days by default (custom clients: 1–90 days). Prompt users to re-authorize before expiry, since a refresh doesn't extend the refresh token itself.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Validity range is sourced. That refreshing doesn't extend the refresh token is our reading; the docs we read don't say.

Implement the per-account OAuth flow with PKCE

blockers.cause: redirect_uri doesn't match OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI / OAUTH_ALTERNATE_REDIRECT_URIS, or is malformed (for example has query parameters).
blockers.fix: Use exactly the stored URI, and add others with OAUTH_ALTERNATE_REDIRECT_URIS.

blockers.cause: The requested role isn't granted to the user, is blocked (for example ACCOUNTADMIN), or the role name's case is wrong.
blockers.fix: Request a non-privileged role that's granted to the user, matching case exactly, or use session:role-encoded for special characters.

blockers.symptom: Token request returns invalid_client although the secret is right
blockers.cause: A network policy on the integration or account blocks your server's IP, or the client credentials are encoded wrongly.
blockers.fix: Have the customer allow your egress IPs in the integration's NETWORK_POLICY, and check Basic auth encoding.

blockers.symptom: Queries fail with 390303 OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_INVALID after about 10 minutes
blockers.fix: Refresh proactively, or have the admin raise OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_VALIDITY (max 3600).

blockers.symptom: invalid_grant on refresh after about 90 days
blockers.cause: The refresh token reached OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY (max 90 days unless Support extends it), or was revoked.
blockers.fix: Send the user through authorization again; ask the customer to request a longer validity from Snowflake Support if needed.

blockers.cause: Wrong account URL or account locator, so the host isn't a real Snowflake account.
blockers.fix: Have the user copy their account URL from Snowsight (account menu) and validate it before redirecting.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: A made-up account host returned HTTP 404 'File not Found' for /oauth/authorize on 2026-10-20; we didn't test a real account.

nuances.text: Access tokens default to 10 minutes (60–3600 s configurable). Refresh tokens default to 90 days (custom clients 1–90 days); going outside that range needs a Snowflake Support request.
IS_AGENTIC = TRUE marks every session from the integration as an AI agent session (IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED returns TRUE), which customers can use in policies or auditing.
ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN, ORGADMIN and GLOBALORGADMIN are blocked from OAuth by default, so an agent can't run as an admin unless the customer changes account settings.

For SaaS clients the token request comes from your public servers, so use the customer's public account URL even if they use PrivateLink; USE_PRIVATELINK_FOR_AUTHORIZATION_ENDPOINT can keep the browser step private.
Security admins can pre-approve consent for users (ALTER USER ... ADD DELEGATED AUTHORIZATION) or via PRE_AUTHORIZED_ROLES_LIST for confidential clients, which removes the consent prompt.
Partner integrations (Tableau, Looker, Alation, ThoughtSpot, Collibra) use predefined OAUTH_CLIENT values; the docs don't describe a path for a new vendor to become one.
